heading: The maternal lines
lead: Five women married into this line and carried it forward, and for years the front page said the same thing under each of them: «no archive of her own line yet». David asked on 29 September 2026 for that to stop being true. These are the pages; the research behind them is mostly still to do, and each page says exactly how much.

salomon.name: Salomon
salomon.gen: Generation two — she married Giovanni Battista Defranceschi (1787–1846).

sections.h2: What is documented is one line, and it is the marriage
paras: She was born **17 March 1797** at **Gračišće**, and she married **[Giovanni Battista Defranceschi](/direct-line/)**, born 1787, died 1846. *(**doc**.)*

**That is the whole of it.** No parish entry for her marriage and no death. *Her parents and siblings are now a **candidate**, from the Gračišće baptism book read on 16 November 2026: it is the section **«Her baptism is on the reel the family holds»** further down this page, and it is **inf**, not doc.* She is generation two, and she is the thinnest woman on this line — which is why the one thing the family *said* about her people mattered so much, and why it had to be tested rather than repeated.

sections.h2: The family remembered two things about the Salomon, and only one of them was theirs
paras: The archive's pedigree carries a note about her *family* rather than about her: *«Of a family with a **palace on the square facing the bishop's**; by **1848** a **Salomon sat in the parliament at Vienna**.»*

**So the Salomon of Gračišće were not peasants** — a house with a building on the main square and, within a generation of Francisca, a seat in the Reichstag. **That note had no source attached to it.** One half of it now has one. The other half turned out to belong to somebody else.

sections.h2: The palace is real, and it is dated 1570
paras: The **Salamon palace at Gračišće** stands on the square, is of the **sixteenth century — the date 1570 is given** — and its distinguishing feature is a row of **Gothic bifore**, Venetian two-light windows, on the first floor. It is in poor condition and wants restoration.

*(**doc** for the building. The source describing it **gives no family history and cites nothing**, so it establishes the palace and not the people. That a house on that square carries the name is not the same as a documented line from it to Francisca, and this page does not pretend otherwise.)*

sections.lab: Withdrawn 29 September 2026 · the official roll of the first Austrian Reichstag, 1848–49
sections.h2: No Salomon sat in that parliament — and the seat the family remembered was their own
paras: **David downloaded the roll of the 422 deputies himself**, and it was read here the same hour. *(The obstacle had been mechanical and on this session's side: the file resists text extraction and the browser pane is served it as a download. It was never a closed door.)*

**There is no Salomon in it.** And the negative is made properly, because a nil is only worth the list behind it: **437 lines, 65 surnames beginning with S, zero matches for Salomon or Salamon in any spelling** — with the control passing, since the S-names parse correctly and are listed. *(**doc** for the negative.)*
**And the seat was real. It was this family's.** The roll reads, verbatim:
> **Defranceschi · Karl · k.k. Rathsprotokollist · Pisino · Küstenland**

**[Carlo De Franceschi](/carlo/) of Gologorica, the historian, sat for the district of Pisino — Pazin.** The archive already half-knew it: Carlo's page has said since 13 September that he «sat in Vienna» and was a *Rathsprotokollist des Landrechts zu Rovigno* — but that came from a **newspaper attacking him**, the Journal des Österreichischen Lloyd of 7 September 1848. This is the official roll, it confirms the office, and it adds what the newspaper never gave: **the seat he was elected for.**

**A family remembered a parliamentary seat correctly for a century and a half and attached it to the wife's people instead of its own.** The Salomon note loses its parliament and keeps its palace. [The correction is recorded.](/corrections/)

sections.lab: Three doors, and what is behind each
sections.h2: What is not known, and is worth asking for

asks.a: **The baptism of 17 March 1797 at Gračišće is on a reel this family already holds, and it was read on 16 November 2026**: DAPA ZM34K-215, frame M01070211, house 132, **Joannes Salamon** and **Maria Salamon**, godparents Franciscus and Joanna Picot ([the section below](/maternal/salomon/) has the entry). **What is still open is the child's name cell**, which the photograph does not settle (a clean «Anna» under a struck «Maria», and a fainter word above them that looks like «…ncisca»). *An earlier version of this page said the baptism was on the reel not held and needed a letter: that was wrong for 1797.* The reel that is **not** held, ZM34K-216 (after the «NASTAVLJA SE» card), holds the 1819 baptism of her **daughter** and the later books, not hers.
Not found. Giovanni Battista's own status animarum line gives *matrimonium 1819*, so the entry should sit in the Gračišće marriages of that year — in the same books, behind the same closed door.

asks.q: And the book that would probably answer all of it at once
asks.a: **[Miroslav Bertoša, «Gologorički De Franceschi: između etosa i etnosa»](/sources/), 1985** — seventy-six pages on this family by one of Croatia's leading historians of Istria, which this archive's own source list calls «the most important single thing still unread». **Not online.** A Croatian library or an interlibrary loan. A study that long of the household Francisca married into is the likeliest single place for her marriage, her family and the palace to be discussed together.

sections.lab: Gračišće baptisms, 26 November 1807 · DAPA ZM34K-215, M01070226
sections.h2: A widow Salamon stands godmother at Gračišće, ten years after Francisca was born there
paras: **This is the first Salamon this archive has found inside a Gračišće parish register.** *Everything before it came from a building, a printed history or a surname database.*

> At the baptism of **26 November 1807**, house 203, of a daughter Catharina to Antonius Bicol and Maria *olim* Iuxa, the godparents are *«Franciscus Jurich»* and *«**Maria vidua Salamon**»* — **Maria, the widow Salamon.** *(doc.)*

**Francisca Salomon was born on 17 March 1797.** *A widow of the name standing at the font in the same parish ten years later is the right generation to be her mother, and **that is exactly as far as this goes**. The register gives the widow no forename beyond Maria, no house and no husband. **No kinship is claimed, and none should be read into the coincidence of a surname in a small parish.*** *(Added 16 November 2026: the Gračišće baptism book of 1746–1808 shows a **Maria Salamon as the wife of Joannes Salamon of house 132** in nine baptisms from 1783 to 1802, and Joannes is not met again after 1802. A widow Maria of that household is possible, and it is **inf** only; the 1807 entry itself still gives no husband.)*

**What would settle it was one page, and the page is on the reel the family holds.** *Francisca's baptism of 17 March 1797 sits on frame **M01070211** of **ZM34K-215**, whose baptism book runs to 1807 — this paragraph used to say it lay beyond the **«NASTAVLJA SE»** card, on **ZM34K-216**, and that was wrong. [The entry is told in the next section](/maternal/salomon/).*

sections.lab: Gračišće baptisms 1746–1808 · DAPA ZM34K-215, M01070133–M01070226 · read 16 November 2026
sections.h2: Her baptism is on the reel the family holds: house 132, Joannes and Maria Salamon, with the child's name cell unsettled
paras: **The 1746–1807 baptism book of Gračišće was read end to end for Salamon and Fernasar on 16 November 2026** *(four readers, each frame in three bands, every Salamon- or Fernasar-like word zoomed; the readers' pages are first passes; the 17 March 1797 entry was read again by this session at a larger magnification).* It is the book on the reel the family holds, and it contains the entry for the day this archive has carried as Francisca's birth since the status animarum of Gallignana gave it (house 5, **«born 17 March 1797»**).

> **17 March 1797**, house **132** *(M01070211, left page bottom, right page bottom)*: father **«Joannes Salamon»**, mother **«Maria Salamon»**, godparents **«Franciscus Picot»** and **«Joanna Picot»**, *cives*, baptised by **Antonius Picot, curatus**. **The child's name cell does not settle:** a lightly written word above the line that reads «…ncisca», then **«Maria» struck through**, then a clean **«Anna»**. *(doc for the entry and the parents; the name is **not read**.)*

**Why it is the candidate and not yet the answer.** The day, the month, the year and the surname all agree with the status animarum, and no other child of that day is a Salamon: that is **inf**. The cell, however, reads **Anna**, not Francisca, and the lighter word above it could be show-through from the other side of the leaf as well as an earlier name. *A second exposure of the same opening, or a look at the original leaf, is what would decide it.*

**The household.** Baptisms of **Joannes and Maria Salamon at house 132**, read in the book *(**doc** for each entry; the 1795 entry was checked again at zoom by this session)*:

| date | child | godparents |
|---|---|---|
| 10 Aug 1783 | Maria | Josephus Vuxa, Nothburga Jerbulla |
| 20 Mar 1786 | Maria | Joannes Flora, Franciscus Picot |
| 11 Nov 1787 | Antonius | Sebastianus Rovis, Andriana Rovis |
| 26 Mar 1790 | Catharina («Lucia» written above) | Mathias Bergliaffa, Sancta Bergliaffa |
| 3 Oct 1792 | Rosalia | Simon Balde, Philippa Balde |
| 14 Mar 1795 | **Josepha Francisca** | Joannes Millotich, Barbara Millotich |
| **17 Mar 1797** | **«Anna» (cell unsettled; see above)** | Franciscus Picot, Joanna Picot |
| 16 Oct 1798 | Joannes | Antonius Picot, Theresia De franceschi |
| 22 Jan 1802 | Catharina | Georgius (?), Joanna Madancich |

*A first child named Maria is followed three years later by another Maria, and a Catharina by another Catharina, which is how a name was handed on after an infant died (**inf**). A **Josepha Francisca** of 1795 and the entry of 1797 would fit that pattern; this page does not decide which child grew up to marry in 1819.* A second Salamon couple, **Josephus and Dominica**, is also entered at house 132 *(a «Maria» on 23 Jan 1790, unsettled reading; a **Francisca on 21 Jan 1792**)*.

**Her mother's maiden name, once, on one cell.** *The 16 October 1798 entry of this house writes the mother **«Maria Salamon n. Picot»** — «n.» for nata — and the godparents are **Antonius Picot** and **Theresia De franceschi**; the priest who baptised most of these children, **Antonius Picot, curatus**, shares the name.* *(doc for the cell, which was zoomed; that **Maria née Picot is Francisca's mother** rests on the house and the date only: **inf**.)* **Franciscus and Joanna Picot** are the godparents of the 1797 entry itself.

**A Defranceschi beside them, not claimed.** A **Theresia De franceschi** stands godmother in three entries of the Salamon households *(26 Feb 1798 house 83; 16 Oct 1798 house 132; 2 May 1802 house 174)*, and a Joannes and a Theresia De franceschi on 9 May 1801. **No relationship is claimed**; it is recorded because Francisca married into the family in 1819 and a later session should not have to find it twice.

**The wider Salamon picture at Gračišće, 1746–1808**, from the readers' lists: the book carries Salamon households at a small number of houses throughout — **Antonius and Catharina** (children 1759–1770: Francisca, Josephus, Antonius, Petrus, Nicolaus); a **judex Joannes Salamon**, whose wife Joanna is godmother in 1747, 1750 and 1755; **Joannes and Maria** (house 132, above); **Petrus** and Juliana (house 32); **Nicolaus** and Maria (house 83); and **Josephus** and Dominica (house 132). Which of them were brothers, and which was the father of Joannes of house 132, is **not established**; the *judex* is mentioned because the family note speaks of a palace on the square, and **nothing ties him to it**.

**This gives worklist 174 something to test.** The «**Antonio Salamon et Maria soror**» who stood godparents at Gologorica in 1843 *([above](/maternal/salomon/))* would be the **mother's own kin** of that baby, who was born to Antonius Defranceschi and **Francisca, daughter of Giovanni Battista and Francisca Salomon of house 5**. The book has an **Antonius** born to Joannes and Maria in **1787** and sisters named **Maria** (1783, 1786): that **fits** and is the only thing it does; there is also an Antonius born 1765 to another couple. **inf only.**

**What was not read.** The binding margins were not read; frame **M01070134** (a loose 1867 sheet over the page, read on the neighbouring frame), the title card and spine photograph, and the «NASTAVLJA SE» card **M01070227** are not register pages; the readers worked at band level and zoomed only the Salamon- and Fernasar-like words. **The row is walked:false.** The **death of Joannes Salamon** and the **1819 marriage** are in books not on this reel.

sections.lab: Gologorica Status Animarum 1826, house 11 · DAPA ZM34K-214, M01069337
sections.h2: A Salman four kilometres away — WITHDRAWN: the family is PALMAN
paras: **Walking the Gologorica household book turned up a household under the name SALMAN**, *and it is close enough to this line to have to be written down, and far enough to have to be written down carefully.*

> **«Franciscus Salman»**, ***Sutor*** — *a shoemaker* — **born 27 October 1796**, house 11, married **8 November 1827** to **«Antonia uxor n. Brusich»**, born 21 March 1797. *Six children entered; four died in infancy.* *(doc.)*
**Read at five times magnification the name is S-a-l-m-a-n.** *There is no* **o** *between the* l *and the* m. *It is not written Salomon and it is not written Salamon.*

**⚠ So nothing is claimed.** *What is recorded is the coincidence, because a later session should not have to find it twice: a **Salman** born **October 1796** at **Gologorica**, four kilometres from **Gračišće**, where the **Salamon palace** stands and where **Francisca Salomon** was born in **March 1797**. **Five months and four kilometres.**

**What would settle it was her baptism**, *which names her father — and it has now been read, on the reel the family holds (16 November 2026; see the section «Her baptism is on the reel the family holds» below): the candidate is a **Joannes Salamon of Gračišće house 132**. Among the baptisms of that house the readers listed there is no child born in October 1796, and the **Palman** reading above stands.*

**⚠ WEAKENED THE NEXT DAY, BY READING ON.** *The Gologorica baptism book, folio 44, enters a* **«Lucia PALMAN»** *on 7 January 1808, daughter of* **Stephanus Palman** *and Catharina née Jurich — and at five times magnification that initial is an unmistakable* **P**, *with a closed bowl and a descender.* *(doc — ZM34K-214, M01069057.)*

**Both readings survive the test, and that is the point.** *The 1826 initial was re-checked against the same scribe's own hand: it matches the* **S** *of* «Sutor» *written on the very same line. **So the 1826 book really does say Salman, and the 1808 book really does say Palman.**

*Almost certainly one family, spelled two ways by two scribes eighteen years apart — and if the earlier form is* **Palman**, *then the resemblance to* **Salomon** *is a coincidence of one hand, not a clue.* **The lead is not withdrawn, because the 1826 reading stands; it is downgraded, because the 1808 reading exists.** *Recorded rather than quietly dropped, since it was published here yesterday.*

**❌ WITHDRAWN, 5 October 2026. The family is PALMAN, and the 1825 entry names his father.**

> *«**Franciscus PALMAN filius Stephani, Sutor**», with* «Antonia ejusdem uxor nata Brusich» — *the baptism of their daughter Maria, 12 July 1825, house 28.* *(doc — ZM34K-214, M01069092.)*

**That settles it, because it is a patronymic and not just a spelling.** *The man the 1826 census writes* «Salman» *is here written* **Palman** *and named* ***filius Stephani*** — *tying him to the* **Stephanus Palman** *who appears in this register from* **1799**, *with children Theresia (1799) and Lucia (1808) and a wife Sancta and later Catharina née Jurich.* **Three entries write P and name a father; one writes S.**

**So there is no Salman at Gologorica, and no coincidence to record.** *The lead published on 30 September and downgraded on 1 October is now **withdrawn entirely**. [The correction is here](/corrections/). **This line still has no register entry of its own**, and the thing that would give it one is still Francisca Salomon's own baptism of 1797, on the Gračišće reel [the family does not hold](/errands/).*

sections.lab: Gologorica baptisms, 15 November 1843 · DAPA ZM34K-214, M01069118
sections.h2: A Salamon stands godfather to a Defranceschi child — and this time the word was tested first
paras: **This archive published a «Salman» of Gologorica on 1 October, downgraded it on 4 October and [withdrew it entirely on 5 October](/corrections/)**: *the family was* **PALMAN**, *and a patronymic —* «Franciscus Palman **filius Stephani**, Sutor» — *settled it.* ***Six days of public error, because the word was written up before it was tested.***

**On the same day a second Salamon-shaped word turned up in the same book, and the order was reversed.** *At the baptism of* **Teresia Defranceschi**, *15 November 1843, house 5 — daughter of Antonius Defranceschi and Francisca — the godparents are entered* **«Antonio SALAMON et Maria soror»**, *conditio* **cives**.

**THE TEST, before anything was claimed.** *[A hand is only legible against itself](/method/). The scribe is* **Petrus Milcetich**, *and he writes* «Franciscus **Palman** sutor» *eleven folios earlier, on 28 April 1841. Both words were cut from the film* **at one magnification** *and set one above the other — [the plate is published on the Gologorica page](/gologorica-line/) so a reader can check the archive rather than take its word:*

| | Palman, 1841 | Salamon, 1843 |
|---|---|---|
| **initial** | *a tall closed majuscule bowl, the same form as his* **B** *in* «Brussich» | *a small low pointed stroke, no bowl* |
| **body** | *a · l · m · a · n* | *a · l · **a** · m · **o** · n* |
| **letters** | six | seven |
***The medial «a» between the l and the m is the clincher: Palman has nothing there.*** **The 1843 word is not Palman.** *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069118, folio 104.)*

**⭐ WHY IT MATTERS ON THIS PAGE.** *A Salamon surname at Gračišće was already established here — [the widow Salamon standing godmother in 1807](/maternal/salomon/) and the palace on the square.* ***This is a Salamon four kilometres away at Gologorica, entered* **civis**, *with* «Maria soror» *beside him — a household, not a stray name — standing for a Defranceschi child.***

**⚠ AND WHAT IT IS NOT.** *Nothing ties this Antonio Salamon to Gračišće, and nothing ties him to* **[Francisca Salomon](/maternal/salomon/)**. *A shared surname four kilometres apart in Istria is a direction, not a descent.* ***What would make it a line is Antonio Salamon tied to Gračišće***, *and [worklist 174](/worklist/) sets out the order of work — sweep this baptism book for the name it was never read for, then the 1826 household index, then the death register at two per cent read, and only then Gračišće on the reel the family does not hold.*
**This is the first lead on this line that has survived its own test.** *It is recorded as a lead and nowhere as a connection.*

tree.caption: Drawn from the direct-line file, which names her as the wife of Giovanni Battista and lists the household's four children. Her own parents are not drawn: no document this archive holds names them. The widow Salamon at the Gračišće font in 1807 is a lead and is not drawn as her mother, because a chart that draws a guess is a confident diagram telling a lie.

fernasar.name: Fernasar
fernasar.gen: Generation three — she married Antonio Defranceschi (1825–1894), the stonecutter of house 19.

paras: Born **17 October 1832** at **Gračišće**. She married **[Antonio Defranceschi](/direct-line/)** the stonecutter on 25 November 1856, and their son **Josip**, born 22 March 1863, is the man who took this line down off the Istrian karst to the Kvarner coast. *(**doc**.)*
Everything else about her turns on four letters, because **two hands wrote her surname and they do not agree**.

sections.lab: The pedigree's own wall note, against a register entry of 1862
sections.h2: Two hands wrote her surname, and they do not agree
paras: This archive's pedigree has carried the flag for a year: *«The surname is written **Fernasar** and **Tornasar** in different hands.»* **An F and a T in a nineteenth-century Istrian hand are not always distinguishable**, and the difference decides which family she belongs to and which entries in the register are hers.

And the second reading is not a copying slip travelling through this archive's own files. **A register entry of 1862 was read «Maria Tornasar»** and is recorded that way. Some scribe, somewhere, formed a letter that a careful reader took for a T. That reading is kept as a reading; what follows is about whether the *name* can be right.

sections.lab: Settled 29 September 2026 · the Austrian press, then two national surname databases
sections.h2: «Tornasar» is retired: it is printed nowhere, and borne by nobody
paras: **The press test came first.** Three spellings were run against the digitised Austrian newspapers. **«Tornasar» returns nothing at all** — not one issue. **«Fernasar» returns three**, and two of them are Austro-Hungarian casualty lists, which print a man's name, rank, regiment, **home commune** and year of birth:
> *Fernasar Josef, Inft., k. k. LIR. Nr. 5, 10. Komp., **Istrien, Pisino, Gračišće**, 1884; kriegsgef., Merw, Gebiet Transkaspien, Rußland.* — «Verlustliste», 6 May 1916

**Josef Fernasar, born 1884, of Gračišće** — taken prisoner and held at Merv in Transcaspia. The list gives province, district and commune, and the commune is **Maria's own village**, named in a printed record fifty-two years after she married out of it. *(A second issue, the wounded list of 14 December 1914, has a Josef Fernasar of the Pisino district born 1883 in hospital at Kassa with a kicked heel. **Whether that is the same man is not settled**: name, district and rough age agree; unit and year do not. Two cousins would look exactly the same.)*

**Today the question was put to two national surname databases**, because [the work list](/worklist/) predicted an atlas would decide the letter from the armchair. The full list of terms tried, with a control on each, is [in the search log](/searched/). In short: the **Croatian 2011 census** returns fewer than ten bearers — or none, it will not say which — for **Fernasar, Tornasar, Fernazar and Fornasar** alike, while returning **757 Poropat**; and **Cognomix**, which holds about 180,000 Italian surnames, has **no Fernasar and no Tornasar at all**.

**So the prediction was wrong, and it is worth saying so.** No atlas of the present can choose between two names that have both stopped existing. What the databases do is remove Tornasar's last possible support: it is borne by nobody in either country and printed in no issue of anything. **The reading stands as Fernasar** — on the press, not on the palaeography, which is still unread. *(**inf**, and firmly held.)*

**The person id is not changed.** `maria-fernasar-tornasar-de-franceschi` was minted when the question was open, and [ids are frozen here](/method/): a moved id is a dead URL. The id records what this archive believed when it minted it, which is the point of freezing them.

sections.h2: Two Pula marriages, ten years apart, write her name «Tornasar» and «Fornasar»
paras: **On 14 January 1888, in the Pula cathedral, her daughter Leopolda married Emericus Zuban, and the entry names the bride's parents: «Defranceschi Antonius, lapicida» and «Tornasar Maria»** ([the page](/person/leopolda-de-franceschi-1865/); `doc`). Leopolda was born at Gallignana on 6 November 1865 and had been a servant at Pola since 1883. The forename, the trade, the village and the mother's surname all agree with the pedigree's [Antonius](/person/antonius-defranceschi-1825/) and [Maria](/person/maria-fernasar-tornasar-de-franceschi-1832/), so the identification is `inf` and firm.

**This is the first time the surname has been read as an image rather than as an index row — and the hand is large and clear.** The method on this page's own list was to compare the doubtful letter with the *same scribe's* capital T and capital F on the same page. The scribe's **F** — «Franceschini» in the witness column, «Föttinger» in the entry beneath — has a **middle bar**. The first letter of the mother's surname is a top bar and a stem, with none. **It is a T.** ([The comparison, at the greatest enlargement the image allows](/maternal/fernasar/).) A single T-versus-F reading is not a proof — the strokes are short, and an F with a faint middle bar would look like this — but it is a reading, made on the ink, and it points the other way from the press test.

**What it does and does not change.** *It copies a certificate*: the entry's footnotes cite the bride's baptism («fides baptismi sponsae»), so the spelling is that of the **Gračišće priest of 1865**, carried through a Pula copyist in 1888 — one scribe's T, not a village's pronunciation. *It does not reinstate «Tornasar»*: the press test above — three issues of «Fernasar», none of «Tornasar» — still stands as evidence about which name a real family bore; but it was offered as the *reason* to retire the T reading, and **a clear T on a page is the evidence that reading was waiting for**. The honest state is: **the name is written Tornasar at Pula in 1888, Fernasar in the pedigree and the press; the baptism of 17 October 1832 as an image is the tie-breaker, and it has still not been opened.** *(`doc` for the 1888 spelling; the identity of the woman `inf`.)*

**And then the second daughter's wedding, ten years later, settles half of it.** On **31 January 1898**, in the same cathedral, **Catharina** — born at Gallignana on 3 February 1869, a servant at Pola since 1894 — married the porter Joannes Kostessich, and her parents are written «**Defranceschi defunctus Antonius, lapicida**» and «**Fornasar Maria**» ([the page](/person/catharina-defranceschi-kostessich-1869/); `doc`). **The first letter has a middle bar — an F** — in a different priest's hand, on a page where «Franciscus» and «Stephanus» are written by the same pen beside it. **So the same woman is «Tornasar» in 1888 and «Fornasar» in 1898, and «Fernasar» in the pedigree: three readings, two scribes, one mother.** The 1898 reading is the one the newspapers and the Friulian *fornasâr* (the kiln-man) already pointed to — **49 issues of «Fornasar» against none of «Tornasar»** — so the weight now falls on **Fornasar** (`doc` for the 1898 spelling; `inf` for the woman, the pedigree's Maria). *The 1888 T is still a T on the page; it is one scribe's letter, and a copyist's slip from F to T is the simplest account. The 1832 baptism as an image, in the Gračišće book, remains the tie-breaker — and an Antonius who is already «defunctus» in 1898 sits comfortably with the tree's 1894.*

*Also on the page:* her daughter's **marriage came five years after Leopolda went into service at Pola** (from 1883), and the groom, Zuban — corrected in a footnote to **Zuppan** — was a carpenter from Pirano. Nothing on the page links the couple to the Pola Defranceschi household of [Franciscus Liberatus](/households/), her father's brother.

sections.lab: fornasâr — the man who works the kiln
sections.h2: And the commoner form of the name points at Friuli
paras: Beside the three Fernasar issues, the Austrian press holds **49 issues of «Fornasar»**, overwhelmingly in the same Pola paper. Fornasar is very probably the same name: Friulian ***fornasâr***, the man who works the kiln — a trade name, like *lapicida* on the other side of this marriage.

**And Fornasar is alive where that etymology says it should be.** Cognomix gives it about **25 families in Italy**: **Piemonte 11, Friuli-Venezia Giulia 8, Veneto 4, Liguria 1, Puglia 1**. Twelve of the twenty-five are in Friuli and the Veneto, which is the corner of Europe the word comes from. In Croatia it is under ten, like the rest — **the name did not stay in Istria**.

*The eleven in Piemonte are not explained here. Industrial migration to the north-west is the obvious reading and is **inf**, not doc.* And the step from Fernasar to Fornasar is itself still **inf**: two spellings in the same newspapers of the same province is a strong hint and not a document.

**A Fornasar household of Gallignana was baptising at Pola in 1878.** *On 30 June 1878 «Joannes», born on the 25th, was baptised in the Pola cathedral, son of «Fornasar Antonius, Antonii, e Gallignana, auriga» (a carter) and «Skubla Francisca, Joannis, e Gallignana»; the sponsors were Ravasini Florentius, lanius, and Grossi Catharina* ([the entry](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899F-79QK?cc=2040054&wc=9R26-BZQ); Pula births 1874–87, entry 345, house 1; `doc`). **It spells the name with an F, in the same register that a decade later copies «Tornasar» for Maria** — and from the same parish. *No kinship to Maria Fernasar is claimed: the entry gives no further generation, and this was found while reading the register for the surname Defranceschi, not for hers.*

sections.lab: Gračišće baptisms 1746–1808 · DAPA ZM34K-215, M01070133–M01070226 · read 16 November 2026
sections.h2: The Fernasar of Gračišće before Maria: four households by 1778, a cluster at houses 152 and 153 by 1800
paras: **The question this page asked, «where are the Fernasar households at Gračišće?», has a first answer.** *The baptism book of 1746–1807 on the reel the family holds was read for the name by four readers on 16 November 2026; every Fer-, For-, Ver- and Ter- word was zoomed. These are the readers' entries, not re-read one by one (the 16 March 1797 entry was checked again by this session: **«Marinus Fernasar»**, house 152).*

**In the book the name is Fernasar, Fernazar or Fornasar, and the initial is F in every zoom.** *The same household is written Fernasar and Fernazar in different years, and Fernasar and Fornasar in 1752 and 1754; the first vowel is often not settled in the hand. No **Tornasar** and no **Vernasar** was read in this book (**doc** for this book only: the Pula copies above still write «Tornasar», and a copyist is not the Gračišće priest).*

**Before house numbers, 1746–1778** *(prose entries, no numbers):* a **Marinus Fernasar** and his wife stand godparents again and again from 1746 to 1775; **Matthaeus and Helena** (children 1748, 1752 and 1754); **Franciscus and Agnes** (1747, 1749, 1754, 1761); and **Antonius and Maria**, whose baptisms run from 1767 to 1777. *The Fernasar are an old Gračišće name, not a newcomer's.*

**With house numbers, 1779–1808**, as the readers read them:

| house | Fernasar parents entered | baptisms seen |
|---|---|---|
| 152 | Marinus (wife Dominica or Maria); Joannes and Gregoria | 1793–1806 |
| 153 | Georgius and Apolonia; Simon (wife Apolonia, Dominica or Catharina) | 1784–1803 |
| 196 | Josephus and Maria (to 1791), then Marinus and Antonia | 1779–1803 |
| 146 | Vitus «alias Valle» and Joanna | 1790–1800 |
| 147 | Matthaeus and Helena (then Antonia) | 1784–1794 |

*The number is sometimes read 193 for 153 and the wives' names vary from entry to entry in one house, which the readers flagged and this session did not settle (**inf** for any couple).*

**What it does not give.** Maria was born in **1832**, twenty-five years after the book on this reel ends, so her parents are not in it, and **no entry here names her** — the link between her and any of these houses rests on the surname and the parish only. *No relationship is claimed.* **What would test it:** the Gračišće baptism book after 1807 (ZM34K-216), or the status animarum of the 1830s–60s, which gives her house number.

sections.lab: Four doors, and what is behind each
sections.h2: What is not known, and is worth asking for

asks.q: What letter did the priest actually form?
asks.a: **Her own baptism, 17 October 1832, at Gračišće — read as an image, not from an index.** Everything above is about whether the name can be right; none of it is about the ink. [The method this archive uses on a doubtful letter](/method/) is that a hand is only legible against itself: find the same scribe writing both candidate letters elsewhere in the same book, and compare at one magnification.

asks.q: Where are the Fernasar households at Gračišće?
asks.a: **Found in the baptism book, not yet at Maria's own house.** *The Gračišće baptism book of 1746–1808 was read for Fernasar on 16 November 2026 ([the section above](/maternal/fernasar/)): Fernasar households baptise there throughout, mainly at houses **152 and 153**, with others at **196, 146 and 147**.* **Which of them was Maria's father's house has not been found:** her own baptism (1832) lies beyond the end of the held book (1807), and nothing yet ties her to a house. **Josef of 1884** is two generations below Maria.

asks.q: What is in the third Fernasar issue?
asks.a: ***Il Giornaletto di Pola*, 8 December 1914** — the one issue of the three that has never been read.

asks.q: A marriage in November, an eldest son in August
asks.a: The marriage is recorded **25 November 1856** and the eldest son Antonius is born **6 August 1856**, three and a half months earlier. Both dates are documented twice. This is a separate puzzle and it is not solved by settling the surname.

childMarks.Antonius: born before the marriage on record — open

tree.caption: Drawn from the direct-line file, which names her as the wife of Antonio and lists the household's five children. The first child, Antonius, is entered at 6 August 1856 and the marriage at 25 November 1856; both dates are documented twice and the gap is an open question on this page, not a settled fact. Her own parents are not drawn: no document this archive holds names them.

kovacina.name: Kovačina
kovacina.gen: Generation five — she married Anton Rudolf Defranceski (1890–1943), born at Klenovica house 22.

rows.lab: What is documented — and now it is her own parish's paper
rows.text: **Her baptism, read on 27 October 2026** (Crikvenica births 1859–1896, page 246, entry 12, image 652 (DGS 5494727 frame 653) of waypoint 9R28-RMH, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-R9M9-1?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-RMH%3A391644801%2C391675201%2C391676801)): «*Uršula*», **born 28 February 1895, baptised 2 March**, **nezakonita** — illegitimate — to «*Marija Car, ćer Vjekoslava i Vinke, radnica*». *(doc, level 13.)* **No father and no surname are entered.** Her mother married **Petar Kovačina, a joiner of house 119, on 28 October 1895** — eight months later — and no legitimation by that marriage is written in the remarks. Her sister **Josipa** (same mother) died at 18 months on 10 September 1898. *(doc.)* **And a margin note in a later hand gives her death: «umrla 3.XI.1975 u Beogradu»**, from a notice of the Belgrade municipality of Palilula dated 24 February 1976, entered 31 December 1976. *(doc.)*

rows.lab: ⚠ Two things this archive had wrong, and the one it still cannot say
rows.text: **«About 1890» was never a birth date** — it was the German certificates' estimate, and she was **born in 1895**. **And the archive looked in the wrong year for her baptism**: it read the 1896 births and concluded that the years she was likely born in «are not filmed» — because it assumed she was born *after* her parents' marriage of 28 October 1895. She was born eight months **before** it, in a volume that is on film. *(correction, /corrections/.)* **The «24 February» of both online trees is the date of the Belgrade notice, not of her death** — she died on **3 November 1975**. *(inf.)* **What the register still does not say is who her father was.** The Geni World Family Tree names **Petar Kovačina** (`lore`); the baptism names no one.

rows.lab: What the online trees add — graded as trees
rows.text: The Geni World Family Tree (`lore`; it shows no sources, and our own MyHeritage tree repeats its dates with no sources, so they are one witness) gives her mother as **Maria Stipanić née Car**, three sisters (**Josipa**, **Slava Stipanić née Kovačina**, **Jakomina Alafetich née Kovacina**), a marriage to Anton Rudolph Defranceschi at Crikvenica on **21 June 1912**, burial at Crikvenica, and five children. The marriage and the sisters are **leads, not findings**: the first needs the Crikvenica marriage register of 1912, the second a search under Stipanić and Alafetić.

**The Crikvenica marriage of 21 June 1912** (is it filmed, or only at Rijeka?); **the later Crikvenica births**, for her sisters Slava and Jakomina, who would show whether the father of those girls is Petar; and **the Belgrade side**: the Palilula municipality's register of deaths for 3 November 1975, and why she and her daughter Anka Nera were at Belgrade in 1944 and 1975. **The [1948 window](/1948/) and the Arolsen CM/1 file are no longer the only door to her.**

tree.caption: Her mother is drawn from the Crikvenica baptism of 1895 (doc), which enters her as illegitimate and names no father; the Geni World Family Tree names Petar Kovačina, whom her mother married eight months later, and that is lore, so he is not drawn. Her death is a later-hand margin note on that baptism. The five children are those the direct-line file lists for the household of Anton Rudolf; the file does not say which of them were Uršula's.
